title: Figure 1. Five benchmark records that look more comparable than they are
claim: Release stage and adjustment basis change what an employment revision means. Each row is a separate published record, and the rows are not combined.
columns: Did it update the official series?
rows: No. It previewed the later benchmark.
Compare with the final benchmark revision only as a change between stages.

March 2025 total revision against the previously published estimate

Do not substitute for a not seasonally adjusted row; seasonal processing differs.
No. The final benchmark is scheduled for February 2027.
scope: National CES total nonfarm employment, March 2025 and March 2026 benchmarks.
units: Revision level in jobs and the published percent revision.
denominator: The corresponding total nonfarm employment estimate for each record, as defined by BLS. The percentages are transcribed and not recomputed from rounded values.
date: Releases from 9 September 2025 to 28 August 2026, observed 1 October 2026.
transformation: Published levels and percentages are transcribed. The only computed value is the 50,000 difference between the final and preliminary not seasonally adjusted March 2025 benchmark revisions (minus 861,000 less minus 911,000). Years, industries and adjustment bases are not averaged.
uncertainty: Published figures are rounded. The March 2026 value is preliminary. Detailed industries can revise differently from the total.
limitations: Two benchmark years are examples. They are not a trend, an accuracy distribution, a performance score or a political comparison.
doesNotProve: Monthly job losses, the final March 2026 value, any motive, or that one adjustment basis is better than the other.
alt: Table of five benchmark records for March 2025 and March 2026, giving release date, adjustment basis, published revision, whether the official series was updated, and the limit on comparing each row.
